title: Workflow runs consume the entire session WebSearch budget, leaving the main loop unable to do simple follow-up searches
details:
- **What happened:** Two `/deep-research` Workflow runs (104 and 106 agents, ~8.3M subagent tokens total) exhausted the session-wide WebSearch cap. Subsequent WebSearch calls from the main loop returned "this session has used its web search budget (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)". The second run's own caveats reported that nearly every verifier agent also hit the cap before its adversarial contradiction sweep could run, so verification quality silently degraded. WebFetch on guessed URLs then returned 403/404, leaving no path to the requested information.
- **What the user said:** "他妈的，这么多 token 花出去，你连个律师的名字都没找到啊！" (roughly: "damn it, all those tokens spent and you didn't even find one name") — the user asked for a list of primary care doctors near their zip code and received an analysis of insurance referral mechanics with zero named practices.
- **Repro:** Invoke the deep-research workflow twice in one session on research-heavy prompts, then attempt any WebSearch from the main loop. The budget is shared between workflow subagents and the parent session with no reservation or warning as it depletes.
- **Evidence:** Run IDs wf_98405853-eee and wf_1cae7d57-174; workflow task IDs wx22ayiav and wcxiz3k4w; second run's caveats field states "nearly every verifier reported the session WebSearch budget exhausted (200/200) before an adversarial contradiction sweep could run".
- **Cause:** Verified in-session — the WebSearch budget is session-global and shared with workflow subagents; a fan-out workflow can consume all of it, and neither the workflow launch nor the depletion surfaces any warning to the parent. Two contributing model-side errors on my part: routing a "give me a list of local providers" request through a research-and-verify harness at all, and writing args that emphasized mechanism/methodology questions over producing named results.
